chart/check.candidate: Chart check lints the Helm chart with a pinned alpine/helm 3.16.2 container and fails on any lint error
Chart check renders the chart with default values and fails unless the output contains an 'image:' line, then prints OK
Chart check runs helm through Docker, mounting the chart directory, so no local helm install is needed

rbac-auditor/dev-cluster.candidate: `./dev-cluster.sh` (default `up`) creates a kind cluster named `rbac-auditor` (override with CLUSTER) from a pinned node image, unless one with that name already exists
Switches the current kubeconfig context to kind-<cluster> so later auditor runs target the throwaway cluster
Seeds the cluster with kubernetes-goat's deliberately insecure RBAC by shallow-cloning GOAT_REF (default master) into GOAT_DIR, unless that directory already exists, then running its setup script
Stops with 'missing: <bin>' and exit 1 when kind, kubectl, helm or git is not on PATH
`./dev-cluster.sh down` deletes the kind cluster and exits 0
Prints next-step hints ('python3 rbac_audit.py', './dev-cluster.sh down') once the cluster is up
Header comment says the script is 'Not committed' even though dev-cluster.sh is tracked in git; GOAT_REF defaults to the moving `master` branch despite the repo's pin-every-version rule

rbac-auditor/dockerfile.candidate: OCI image labels (title, description, license, source)
HEALTHCHECK NONE for a one-shot CLI
Multi-stage build and per-platform kubectl via TARGETOS/TARGETARCH
Policy module copied beside the script so it can be imported
NOTICE file copied into the image

rbac-auditor/makefile.candidate: make with no target prints every target and its description (help is the default goal)
install installs the package and man page with pip
build tags the image as IMAGE:VERSION
ARGS can be overridden to run diff instead of snapshot
test-unit runs unittest discovery with no Docker or cluster
coverage runs the unit tests under coverage.py and shows missing lines
test runs the unit tests before building the image, then the image smoke tests
lint runs every pre-commit hook on all files
format runs whatever ruff is on PATH, not the pinned one (goes against the CLAUDE.md lint guidance)
analyze refuses with exit 69 and an install link when trivy is missing, otherwise scans for CRITICAL/HIGH vulnerabilities, misconfigurations and secrets
push builds the tagged image and pushes it
release does a multi-arch buildx build for linux/amd64 and arm64 and pushes it tagged with the version and latest

rbac-auditor/rbac-audit.candidate: Rule and grant expansion into per-verb/resource tuples, canonical JSON keys and set lookups
Change records sorted by kind then id within the diff
Sorted directory walk and streamed YAML reading of manifest files
ServiceAccount subjects get their binding's namespace; Group/User subjects get none
Rules granting nothing are dropped from snapshots
Matrix rows are right-trimmed and use ASCII marks for CI logs
Diagnostics go to stderr so `diff > drift.txt` stays clean
Pod ServiceAccount lookup defaults serviceAccountName to default
Snapshot written to stdout by default and 'snapshot written to PATH' logged otherwise
Help text printed and exit 64 when no command is given
Which policy rules fire (cluster-admin, wildcard, escalating verbs, anonymous, masters, unused ServiceAccount) and exemption matching
rbac-auditor/rbac-audit.covered_by: enforced in rbac_audit_policy.py, not this module

rbac-auditor/rbac-audit-policy.candidate: subject_str / grant_str one-line rendering of subjects and grants
CHECKS registry matches DEFAULT_POLICY rule names
evaluation_state builds account sets from the snapshot and live pods
Rules run in sorted name order for a stable output
The first matching exemption entry supplies the reason
null rules / null exempt in the policy file mean none
A user list override replaces rather than extends the default list
The shipped example policy file is valid
Exempted findings keep their fail flag but are never gating
The default ServiceAccount name is shared between snapshot and pod readings

rbac-auditor/dockerfile.rule: The auditor in the image runs as an unprivileged user, not root
The image ships a pinned kubectl only if it matches its published checksum

rbac-auditor/rbac-audit.rule: A snapshot never records when it was taken or which pods ran, so a rollout alone never shows as RBAC drift
A manifest object defined twice is refused rather than guessed at, because apply order would decide which one the cluster gets
Command-line and policy errors are rejected before any cluster read, so a typo never surfaces as a cluster-unavailable failure
